transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get started with the weekly investment review for the finance-system replacement. We've got a proposed $12 million implementation budget, which fits within the board-approved capital plan envelope, and the vendor's schedule runs April through December. Before I make the final budget sign-off, I'd like to hear from each of you on the project conditions. Let's start with accounting — what are you seeing on your end?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Maya, before you make the final budget sign-off, I need to flag something important from an accounting perspective. I confirmed in a memo this morning that exactly 60% of the $12,000,000 project cost — that's $7,200,000 — meets our capitalization criteria. The remaining $4,800,000 would be treated as period expense. I should note that this memo has not yet been circulated to FP&A, so they may not be aware of this split yet.

I received the vendor's countersigned commercial schedule yesterday, and it requires a 20% holdback on each implementation invoice until final acceptance. That effectively means 20% of every invoice — so $2,400,000 of the $12 million — would be retained and not paid out until final acceptance is achieved. I should also note that I have not yet uploaded this countersigned schedule to the procurement repository, so it may not be visible to the rest of the team yet.
